**You need at least 30W, and 65-70W is the best choice if you want faster charging.** Any USB-C charger that supports USB Power Delivery (USB PD) will work.

**What Apple recommends** ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)), for MacBook Air models from 2022 or later:
- **30W** USB-C adapter (13-inch only)
- **35W** dual USB-C port adapter
- **67W or 70W** USB-C adapter

**What ships in the box** (these depend on your model):
- **M5 13-inch (2026):** a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max ([Apple Support](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
- **M4 13-inch (2025):** a 30W adapter with the 8-core GPU, or a 35W dual-port adapter with the 10-core GPU ([Apple Support](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).

**Fast charging:** Apple says it needs a **70W or higher** USB PD source ([Apple tech specs](https://images.apple.com/macbook-air/specs/)). A 65W charger will charge the laptop fine, but it falls short of Apple's fast-charge threshold. Apple also says any USB-C PD adapter works, even if its wattage is higher or lower than recommended. A lower-wattage charger just charges more slowly.

**If you want a third-party option:** the [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W charger](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) is $49.99 as a 2-pack, with two USB-C ports and one USB-A port. Some caveats:
- It's a 65W charger, so it's under Apple's 70W fast-charge mark.
- With two or three devices plugged in, the laptop port drops to 45W. That's still enough for a MacBook Air ([product details](https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u)).
- That link is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission if you buy through it at no extra cost to you.

If you tell me your exact model (13- or 15-inch, and the chip), I can narrow this down. You'll also need a USB-C cable, or the MagSafe 3 cable that came with your laptop, to connect to the charger.
